gloss: to pass through; to cut through

definitions.gloss: to pass through; to cut through
definitions.explanation: To move through and come out the other side of a space, passage, or area. Used for physically traversing tunnels, crowds, forests, and similar spaces.

examples.japanese: トンネルを{通|とお}り{抜|ぬ}けた。
{人混|ひとご}みを{通|とお}り{抜|ぬ}けるのに{苦労|くろう}した。
examples.english: I had a hard time getting through the crowd.

examples.japanese: {裏道|うらみち}を{通|とお}り{抜|ぬ}けると、{駅|えき}まで{五分|ごふん}で{着|つ}ける。
examples.english: If you cut through the back street, you can reach the station in five minutes.

notes:
A compound verb formed from {通|とお}る (to pass) and {抜|ぬ}ける (to come out, to exit). The {抜|ぬ}ける component adds the sense of emerging on the other side. Ichidan conjugation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- トンネルを{通|とお}り{抜|ぬ}ける (to pass through a tunnel)
- {人混|ひとご}みを{通|とお}り{抜|ぬ}ける (to push through a crowd)
- {森|もり}を{通|とお}り{抜|ぬ}ける (to go through a forest)
- {路地|ろじ}を{通|とお}り{抜|ぬ}ける (to cut through an alley)

The particle を marks the space being traversed. Unlike {通|とお}る alone, {通|とお}り{抜|ぬ}ける emphasizes coming out the other side, not just passing along.
